messages:
alex: Thinking out loud: what if we add a 'local fastpath circuit' in the edge proxy to avoid round trips to the global credit allocator for tiny bursts? goal: cut p99 for short chat turns and reduce load on quota service.

jin: sounds useful. how does the circuit decide when to serve from local pool vs call the global allocator?

alex: idea: every edge keeps a small elastic token bucket per-tenant (fastpool). policy: if request <= fastpool_threshold && fastpool_tokens>0 serve locally. otherwise forward. fastpool refills opportunistically from global allocator async.

tara: worried about fairness — local pools could let noisy tenants bypass global throttles. what's the abuse model?
\almatt: (quick comment) +1 to that concern — we need per-tenant probation and dynamic shrink when abuse signals show up.

alex: agreed. defenses: 1) small cap (fastpool_max ~= 0.5% of tenant quota or absolute token cap like 200 tokens) 2) eviction on churn score 3) conservative refill backoff when global signals indicate congestion.

jin: define churn score?

alex: churn = rapid high-frequency allocate+reclaim cycles + high token-consumption variance. simple heuristic: recent_allocs / successful_global_allocs over window. high churn => reduce fastpool_max and increase refill cooldown.

tara: how to implement refill without opening a thundering herd to allocator?
\almatt: staggered backoff with jitter per-edge and per-tenant. also add a leader election among edges for a tenant if multiple edges see deficit so only one edge asks for top-up at a time. leader tie-breaker = sha1(edge_id + epoch) modulo N.

jin: leader election adds complexity. can we instead use probabilistic refills (p=0.05) + capped request size?
\altara: that might be simpler. but leader prevents duplicated allocations that then get revoked. tradeoff.

alex: optional hybrid: leader mode only when tenant has > K concurrent edge connections. otherwise probabilistic refill.

Message: code sketch for fastpool check:

```
// edge request path pseudocode
if (req.tokens <= fastpool_threshold && fastpool.tokens >= req.tokens) {
  fastpool.consume(req.tokens)
  serve_local()
} else {
  resp = await globalAllocator.allocate(req.tokens)
  if (resp.ok) serve_global() else reject_or_queue()
}
```

matt: observability hooks? what metrics and alerts?

alex: per-tenant per-edge: fastpool_tokens, fastpool_topups, fastpool_topup_failures, topup_backoff_seconds, local_hits_pct. global signals: topup_rejections, fastpool_evictions_due_to_churn. alerts: sustained local_hits_pct>40% + topup_rejections>1% => investigate.

jin: interesting — what about correctness/invariants for quota accounting? total issued tokens must match global state eventually.
\altara: here we treat fastpool as a short-lived lease. all local consumes are logged and asynchronously reconciled by sending 'consumed' events to accounting pipeline. reconciliation ensures global totals stay consistent; we accept eventual consistency within short windows.

alex: failure modes: 1) edge crash with unreported consumed tokens -> global allocator may temporarily over-issue. mitigate with per-edge max lease and short lease TTL; require renewal. 2) network partition -> edges should reduce refill rates and rely on local caches.

matt: ops runbook for canary?
\aalex: plan: small canary in eu-west-1 for 48h on low-traffic tenant cohort. Gradually increase fastpool_max (50,100,200 tokens) while monitoring: allocator_qps, topup_rejections, per-tenant SLA error budget, and churn score. Rollback conditions: allocator_qps +10% sustained, or topup_rejections increase >0.5% absolute, or per-tenant latency p99 regresses >5%.

jin: do we need a kill-switch?
\altara: yes: global feature-flag by region + per-tenant override (disable_fastpool). ops-bot can flip flag automatically if alerts fire.

ops-bot: FYI: scheduled canary toggle will be created. auto-alerts for topup_rejections and allocator_qps configured. :robot_face:

jin: next steps: write short RFC with config knobs (fastpool_max, threshold, refill_strategy, lease_ttl, churn_params) + simulations for noisy tenant scenarios. I'll help add SRE checklist.

alex: I'll prototype the edge knob and a unit sim showing how many extra allocator calls fastpool avoids vs worst-case abuse.

matt: thanks, team. small ask: include test plan for partitioned-edge recovery in RFC.

ops-bot: NOTE: created ticket INFRA-9123 for canary rollout and RFC link will be attached.
